answer: Anchor each identity to a registered pearl-oyster lease on a charted reef: the leaseholder's buoy signs a fresh reading each epoch — oyster growth, water temperature, reef photos — bound to the epoch nonce, checked against the public nautical atlas. One lease, one vote; two identities on the same transect collapse to one and burn a $50 stake. One hundred sock-puppets need one hundred real leases at about $400 each plus yearly survey fees, no bulk discount; an honest farmer reuses one lease forever. Replay dies on the fresh nonce; no signed reading, no vote; marginal cost rises linearly in n.
